title: Remove dplyr as dependency
description:
The dplyr requirement is pretty thin, and can be removed I think.

On the one hand, Suggests aren't required to run the package, but OTOH, they can be required for CI, and for that case dplyr is probably too heavy for many downstream use cases, though to be fair a large plurality of such probably use dplyr in their deps closure already...

title: lazy-loaded data are not in the package namespace
description:
Currently, this gives an error:

```
> books <- janeaustenr::austen_books()
Error in janeaustenr::austen_books() : 
  object 'sensesensibility' not found
```

The issue is that [lazy-loaded data are not in the package namespace](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#FOOT58)

This patch puts `janeaustenr::` before the lazy data objects.

title: Make 'dplyr' dependency optional
description:
The Jane Austen texts are great for examples, but requiring `dplyr` can be a real burden. On Travis it takes a considerable amount of time to build and install `dplyr` with all of it's dependencies, while all we really need is the text from Pride and Prejudice.

The current PR changes the `austen_books` function to give exactly the same result, but without using `dplyr`. Therefore the user is no longer forced to install it. `dplyr` can still be used in examples (or vingettes) because it is declared it in `Suggests`.

title: Doc tweaks
lower minimum version of R
description: I want to use your excellent collection of Austen's novels in a teaching environment that only has R v3.1.2.  I don't think there's any particular reason why a higher version is needed, so can we lower the minimum version in case others have similar issues.
